title: Brush Up: The 5-Minute Daily News - AI/Tech, Biz, World
description: Your definitive morning intelligence download. Every day shortly after 7:00 AM EST, we bypass the noise to deliver the critical shifts in AI, Global Business, and Macroeconomics that define the modern landscape. Brush up on the news while you brush up your smile.
latestSummary:
Google acquired cybersecurity firm Wiz for $32 billion, marking a significant shift in tech priorities. Simultaneously, Elon Musk’s xAI is restructuring its AI coding efforts, aiming for accelerated development. A lawyer is warning of potential mass casualty risks linked to rapidly advancing AI chatbots, highlighting ethical concerns. Travis Kalanick launched Atoms, integrating CloudKitchens into a robotics venture focused on mining and transport. Apple reduced App Store commissions in China, a move with potential global economic impacts. The FBI is investigating malware in video games on Steam, raising security concerns. Peacock is expanding into AI-driven content and gaming.

In business, Adobe’s stock declined following CEO Shantanu Narayen’s departure, reflecting uncertainty about AI strategy. The EV market is slowing, particularly in China, and geopolitical tensions, including the Iran conflict, are driving market instability and outflows. Disruptions in Brazilian soybean exports to China and the strategic importance of an Ohio factory in the “rare earth war” add to global trade complexities. The IRS is facing workforce reductions, impacting tax processing.

Globally, the Middle East remains unstable with increased U.S. military presence. The repatriation of Iranian sailors killed in a U.S. strike is underway. A deliberate attack on a Jewish school in Amsterdam prompted heightened security measures. The Ukraine conflict continues to raise concerns, and Formula One races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia are likely to be cancelled. Negotiations between the U.S. and Cuba are ongoing, and Iranians are reacting to the new supreme leader’s address.

title: Overnight Market Brief - Bridging the Global Gap. Daily.
description:
While North America sleeps, the global economy keeps moving. Overnight Market Brief is your essential pre-market digest, designed for traders, serious investors, and professionals who need to hit the ground running.
Most North American investors miss 50% of the market story because it happens in Tokyo, Hong Kong, and London. We bridge that gap. Every morning at 8:00 AM ET, we deliver a concise, data-driven breakdown and full global picture in under 10 minutes, just in time for your morning commute.
latestSummary:
Global markets opened sharply lower Friday, March 13, 2026, following a defensive close on Wall Street. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 declined significantly, driven by escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and a strengthening US Dollar. The 10-Year Treasury Yield decreased to 4.254%, while the US Dollar Index rose to 100.077, negatively impacting risk assets.

Asia mirrored this trend, with the Nikkei 225, Hang Seng, and Shanghai Composite all experiencing substantial declines due to regional risk aversion and the dollar’s influence. European markets followed suit, hampered by weaker-than-expected economic data, including high German corporate insolvencies and a drop in Euro area industrial production.

US futures showed a modest rebound, suggesting a technical bounce. Investors are closely watching the Iran conflict, the health of the European economy, and central bank policy, particularly the Bank of England. The market is expected to trade range-bound with a defensive bias, awaiting further developments. Data is delayed and may be inaccurate; conduct your own due diligence.

title: Post-market Recap
description:
Did the market "rally into the close" or "fade the open"? The Post-Market Recap goes beyond the green and red arrows to analyze the structure of the trading day. This daily briefing dissects the inter-market correlations that drove the session.
Every afternoon, we cover:
Macro Causality: Connecting the dots between the 10-Year Yield, the Dollar Index, and Equities.
Tech & AI Pulse: A dedicated segment on the semiconductor ecosystem and Big Tech performance.
Market Breadth: Analyzing Volatility (VIX) and Sector Rotation to gauge genuine institutional sentiment.
Closing Catalysts: Identifying the specific news and data that triggered late-day reversals.
latestSummary:
The Post-Market Recap by AGI Era on March 13, 2026, reported a decisive bearish trend across major indices. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 both declined, while the Dow Jones saw a slight decrease, driven by elevated trading volume reflecting institutional liquidation. Investor anxiety spiked, indicated by a significant rise in the VIX (Fear Gauge) to 27.29, signaling a shift from technical corrections to heightened risk aversion.

Sector rotation favored defensive plays, with Utilities (XLU) gaining nearly 1% while Technology (XLK) lagged, reflecting a move towards safety amid geopolitical tensions and economic uncertainty. The 10-Year Treasury Yield rose to 4.283%, further pressuring growth stocks. Escalating concerns regarding the Iran conflict strengthened the US Dollar Index and pushed Crude Oil prices higher.

Within the Magnificent Seven, Nvidia, Microsoft, Apple, Meta, Amazon, Google, and Tesla all experienced declines, mirroring the broader market rotation away from high-growth tech. This pullback highlighted a shift in investor appetite towards more defensive assets. Looking ahead, key economic data releases, including JOLTS job openings, Consumer Sentiment, and the Core PCE Price Index, will be closely watched. Investors are advised to exercise caution and maintain a defensive strategy due to the prevailing macro headwinds.

title: Geopolitical Updates
description: Beyond the headlines lies strategy. Geopolitical Updates is your daily guide to the evolving global order. Each episode provides a rapid scan of the day's top international stories, followed by a deep-dive analysis of the single most impactful event shifting the geopolitical landscape. From tension in the South China Sea to economic statecraft in Europe, we explain not just what happened today, but why it matters for tomorrow. Delivered daily at 7 PM ET.
latestSummary:
The United States has significantly increased its military presence in the Middle East, deploying an amphibious ready group and additional Marine forces in response to escalating tensions. This move is a direct reaction to the conflict in Ukraine, with Ukrainian President Zelenskyy expressing concerns about Russia exploiting the situation involving Iran.

Simultaneously, Hamas is appealing to Iran to halt attacks on Gulf states, while reiterating Tehran’s right to self-defense against U.S. and Israeli aggression.  Domestic unrest is also rising in Cuba, fueled by a severe energy crisis and U.S. sanctions.

Across Europe, a deliberate attack on a Jewish school in Amsterdam followed a previous security breach in Rotterdam, prompting heightened security measures.  Furthermore, exiled Kurdish fighters in Iraq are preparing for a potential confrontation with Iran, amid ongoing drone attacks. 

The U.S. redeployment signals a strategic prioritization of the Middle East, impacting global oil markets and maritime security. Analysts predict this could lead to a re-evaluation of regional security architectures and potentially shift alliances within the Gulf region. Monitoring Iranian reactions to the U.S. buildup and developments regarding eased Russian sanctions are key priorities.
